content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 1-2% above recent peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to correct; add 0.5-1.0% downward bias for next 3-5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing: if sentiment changes >0.3 in 3 days, adjust forecast by -0.1 to -0.3 of sentiment magnitude.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (e.g., 0.00/0.22/0.69 mix), model often overfits short-term noise; use 3-day moving average of true prices as baseline.
